cats.name: PEPECAT
cats.catName: PEPECAT, the cat with Pepe's face
cats.whoIsTheCat: No real cat. PEPECAT is a cartoon mascot: a charcoal-grey cat drawn with the face of Pepe the Frog (Matt Furie's Boy's Club character), with sleepy green eyes and a wide red grin. It launched on pump.fun on 27 Nov 2024 and is drawn by its Solana community, which names Jaggedsoft and TrystanNFT as founders. The site says it has no affiliation with Matt Furie.

virality.summary: A small, art-driven community, not a single viral moment. PEPECAT was created on pump.fun on 27 Nov 2024 and moved to Raydium about four minutes later. MEXC listed it on 5 Mar 2025. The community keeps an archive of fan art (the site's motto: 'Pepe found the internet. Then the internet gave him a cat.') and an OpenSea collection, PEPECAT Legends. Its pull comes from Pepe the Frog, one of the internet's most-remixed memes. Posts on its own X account are modest: most get a few hundred views.

cats.lore: Pepe found the internet. Then the internet gave him a cat. PEPECAT is that cat: a charcoal kitty with Pepe's sleepy green eyes and a huge red grin, 'moody, loud, endlessly remixable'. He was born on pump.fun on 27 November 2024 and raised by Solana meme-makers. He has no real-life twin. He lives in fan art instead: surfing waves, floating in a sunlit forest pond, exploring a jungle temple with friends. His community keeps every drawing in an archive, because to them PEPECAT is a comic strip that anyone can add to.

cats.name: Keyboard Cat
cats.whoIsTheCat: Fatso was a male ginger tabby owned by artist Charlie Schmidt of Spokane, Washington. In 1984 Schmidt filmed him 'playing' a keyboard in a baby-blue T-shirt, working his paws off-camera. Schmidt posted the clip to YouTube in June 2007. It went viral in 2009 as 'Play Him Off, Keyboard Cat'. Fatso died long ago. Bento, Skinny and, since 2026, Presley carry on the role.

virality.summary: One of the internet's oldest cat memes. Schmidt uploaded the 1984 VHS clip in 2007 as 'charlie schmidt's cool cat'. In February 2009 Brad O'Farrell of My Damn Channel tacked it onto the end of a blooper to 'play off' the person, like the vaudeville hook, and 'Play Him Off, Keyboard Cat' spread across YouTube. Current TV ranked it No. 2 of its 50 Greatest Viral Videos, and Fatso starred in a 2011 Super Bowl ad for Wonderful Pistachios. The Base KEYCAT launched in March 2024. It was licensed by Schmidt in August 2024 and listed on Coinbase on 1 April 2025.
virality.metrics: YouTube 'Keyboard Cat! - THE ORIGINAL!': 95,204,322 views. 'KEYBOARD CAT ORIGINAL CLIP 1984': 21,688,378. '"Play Him Off, Keyboard Cat" by Charlie Schmidt': 11,438,706. All from the YouTube results page, 2026-09-25 ~20:50 UTC. Wikipedia: over 81 million views on the original by Sep 2025. Decrypt (Aug 2024): 77 million. @KeyboardCatReal 'officially licensed' post (29 Aug 2024): 97,078 views, 259 likes. X @KeyboardCatBase: 15,821 followers. GeckoTerminal: 911,005 holders.

coin.launched: 2024-03-26: first Uniswap v2 KEYCAT/WETH pool at 02:40 UTC (DexScreener). Licensed by Charlie Schmidt in late Aug 2024 (Decrypt, 29 Aug 2024). Coinbase trading opened on or after 1 Apr 2025 (Coinbase notice via PANews, 31 Mar 2025).
coin.launchpad: None known: a direct ERC-20 deploy with Uniswap v2 liquidity on Base. Fixed supply of 10,000,000,000.
coin.endorsedByOwner: Yes, licensed. Decrypt (29 Aug 2024) reports that creator Charlie Schmidt and his meme manager Ben Lashes signed a licensing deal with both the Base and the Solana KEYCAT communities, and that Schmidt and Lashes hold 'participation in both coins'. The official @KeyboardCatReal account posted that both are 'now officially licensed Memecoins' (29 Aug 2024), and its bio lists this Base contract. The project site says the IP rights are secured with Schmidt's 'full support and endorsement'.

cats.lore: In 1984, in Spokane, Washington, artist Charlie Schmidt put his ginger cat Fatso in a baby-blue T-shirt and filmed him 'playing' a cheerful tune on a keyboard, with Charlie's own hands hidden in the sleeves. He posted the clip to YouTube in 2007. In 2009 it began 'playing off' bloopers everywhere, and 'Play Him Off, Keyboard Cat' became one of the internet's first great cat memes. Bento, Skinny and now Presley have kept the music going, and since 2024 the Base KEYCAT community has played on under Charlie's license.

cats.name: Wen
cats.catName: Wen, the internet's cutest cat (cartoon mascot)
cats.whoIsTheCat: No real cat. Wen is a cartoon kitten: blue-grey and white, with big turquoise eyes. The WEN community gave the coin this mascot in early 2024. The coin itself is a fractionalized NFT of 'A Love Letter to Wen Bros', a poem posted on 23 Dec 2023 by Meow (@weremeow), co-founder of the Solana exchange Jupiter, who calls himself a cat.

virality.summary: Meow's short poem to everyone asking 'wen token?' was a hit. He turned it into an NFT and split it into a trillion WEN tokens. As the first project on Jupiter's LFG Launchpad (26 Jan 2024), WEN gave 70% of its supply in equal shares to over a million Solana wallets, one of Solana's widest airdrops. By March 2024 the coin had a face: 'This cute cat was born under 2 months ago'. The team then made plush toys with TOYMAK3RS (teased Apr 2024) and put a space-suited Wen on its site. Wen now runs two of X's biggest cat accounts, @ShouldHaveCat and @PostsOfCats.

Meow's 'Immortalizing WEN Culture' launch thread (25 Jan 2024): 2,032,729 views, 3,737 likes. LFG Launchpad post (22 Jan 2024): 1,046,554 views. @wenwencoin 'This cute cat was born under 2 months ago' (26 Mar 2024): 85,149 views. X @wenwencoin: 141,810 followers. @ShouldHaveCat: 4,729,698 and @PostsOfCats: 2,492,785 followers; both bios name @FoundationOfWen. Holders: 206,135 (GeckoTerminal) / 209,026 (Jupiter). All read 2026-09-25 ~20:50-21:05 UTC (fxtwitter API).

coin.launched: 2024-01-26: airdrop claims opened at 10:00 ET via Jupiter's LFG Launchpad (Coinfomania, BitPinas). First Meteora WEN/USDC and WEN/SOL pools at 00:07-00:08 UTC (DexScreener).
coin.launchpad: Jupiter LFG Launchpad (its first project, in beta). Fractionalized through Ovols on the WEN New Standard (WNS). 70% was airdropped equally to 1M+ wallets, 20% went to the launch DLMM pool and 10% to the WEN treasury (Meow's thread).
coin.endorsedByOwner: Created by the poem's author. Meow (Jupiter co-founder) wrote the poem, donated it to Ovols and launched WEN himself. His thread says Jupiter has 'NO affiliation with this project apart from hosting this' and launchpad fees, with a 0.25% team allocation. There is no real cat: the Wen mascot belongs to the Wen project, which calls itself an IP brand.

cats.lore: Wen began as a poem. In December 2023 Meow, co-founder of Jupiter, wrote 'A Love Letter to Wen Bros' for everyone forever asking 'wen token?'. In January 2024 the poem became an NFT, was split into a trillion pieces and handed out in equal shares to more than a million Solana wallets. Meow signs off as a cat, and within weeks the community gave the coin a face: a round-eyed, blue-grey and white kitten with a tiny ':3' smile. Today Wen looks after two of X's biggest cat accounts and wants to be the internet's cutest cat.

cats.catName: Diana, the moon cat of Tsuki
cats.whoIsTheCat: No real cat. Tsuki's mascot is Diana, an anime-style black cat with red eyes and a crescent moon on her forehead. The project site says she is named after the Roman goddess of the moon and reflects the Japanese belief that black cats bring prosperity. She arrived with the Solana coin in May 2024. The team is anonymous.

virality.summary: A niche coin with a cult following and a riddle-style X account. TSUKI ('moon' in Japanese) fair-launched on Solana on 11 May 2024 with its liquidity burned. The account posts cryptic numbers, movie stills and countdowns ('TICK', 'Felinus Prime', '855', '4663'). In September 2026 it leaned into GameStop: Diana posed in front of a GameStop storefront, and the account quoted GameStop's 'Your local GameStop is back' post. It then launched a 'scion' TSUKI paired with tokenized GME stock on Robinhood Chain. That gives it a place among the 'cats of stocks'.
